items.claim: The opening cut is argued as a clean speaker break while two byte-grounded lexical hooks run straight across that seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: Both pointed splices in this row re-collate at byte tier against their cited refs, and the two single-witness SAMEKH marks at oshb:Isa.40.2 and oshb:Isa.40.5 are real and correctly placed; the defect is cross-seam disclosure. The divine-title token אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.9 at BYTE tier, and the two units between them carry the first-person-plural counterpart: לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.3) closes this row's own opening verse, and אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.3 at skeleton tier, its consonants sitting inside the prefixed form. A byte-true title bracket therefore spans oshb:Isa.40.1 to oshb:Isa.40.9 straight across this seam. The calling root hooks the same seam, named by attested form rather than by a bare consonantal digit because the participle is written plene and is not a contiguous match for the three-letter skeleton: וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2) then קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3) then קְרָ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.6) and אֶקְרָ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.6), each byte tier against its own verse. The rejected alternative rests precisely on discontinuity at web:Isa.40.2|web:Isa.40.3 and engages neither hook. Holding the speaker unnamed is correct and byte-sound.

items.claim: The row's principal cohesion evidence, the repeated withering-grass clause, is stated through the English with no Hebrew form and no tier, and it is not byte-recurrent.
items.evidence: Re-collated in both directions, יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ (oshb:Isa.40.7) against oshb:Isa.40.8, and יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ (oshb:Isa.40.8) against oshb:Isa.40.7, reach accent_stripped tier and not byte: letters and vowels agree, the accents differ. The row instead writes of the clause as translated so-and-so, with no splice and no tier label on a recurrence claim, which both leaves the claim untiered and understates real evidence. Quote/gloss parity also slips at the onset: the Hebrew run the row splices for its opening verse carries the whole verse through כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה (oshb:Isa.40.6) while the paired English stops at the second question. Cross-seam, the row splices אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) at its own closing verse without disclosing that this is the middle member of a title bracket whose outer members, אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) and the same token at oshb:Isa.40.9, re-collate against each other at BYTE tier across this row's closing seam. Mark handling is correct: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.5 before the span and at oshb:Isa.40.8 at its close, both single-witness disclosed.

items.claim: The rejected alternative asserts a form-class fact the bytes contradict: neither an imperative nor a feminine-singular addressee carries forward into web:Isa.40.10-Isa.40.11.
items.evidence: The opening splice is byte tier and the feminine-singular reading of the herald address is byte-supported: עֲלִי (oshb:Isa.40.9) and הָרִ֤ימִי (oshb:Isa.40.9) and אִמְרִי֙ (oshb:Isa.40.9) and אַל תִּירָ֔אִי (oshb:Isa.40.9), with second-feminine-singular suffixes on לָךְ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.9) and קוֹלֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.40.9). But the sentence stating that the imperative and the addressee both carry forward unchanged fails against the next two verses, whose finite verbs are third-masculine-singular yiqtol under a presentative: יָב֔וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.10), then יִרְעֶ֔ה (oshb:Isa.40.11) and יְקַבֵּ֣ץ (oshb:Isa.40.11) and יִשָּׂ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.11) and יְנַהֵֽל (oshb:Isa.40.11), each byte tier against its own verse. Neither verse carries an imperative and neither carries a second-person form of any gender, so the imperative cluster stops at oshb:Isa.40.9; the one feminine form in the pair, the participle מֹ֣שְׁלָה (oshb:Isa.40.10), agrees with the feminine noun for his arm standing beside it in the same clause and both witnesses render it of the arm, not of an addressee. Neither verse is spliced at all, so the continuity ground is carried in English alone. Cross-seam, the byte-tier title bracket joining אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) to the same token at oshb:Isa.40.9 straddles this row's opening seam undisclosed, with אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) one verse earlier. Marks at oshb:Isa.40.8 and oshb:Isa.40.11 are correctly placed and single-witness disclosed, and refusing to name the herald is right.

items.claim: The interrogative is used as an intra-unit cohesion argument while the same word-bound interrogative continues across this row's closing seam at three further sites (sweep: 3 verses), undisclosed.

items.claim: The envelope driver is a real and exclusive object, but it is tier-labeled byte when the two verses do not recur at any tier.
items.evidence: Both splices are byte tier against their own verses and the swept object is genuinely exclusive: contiguous liken-root forms occur in exactly 2 verses across chs 40-41 (sweep: 2 verses), oshb:Isa.40.18 and oshb:Isa.40.25. The recurrence itself, however, is labeled byte: re-collated, וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18) against oshb:Isa.40.25, and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25) against oshb:Isa.40.18, both return tier NONE, the verbs differing in the dagesh and in the first-person suffix. The row's own closing splice carries the speaker frame יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.40.25) yet the signal list names no speech-formula or divine-title key; the row is nonetheless right not to count that bare epithet as a Holy-One-of-Israel title site, and the two objects are separable in the bytes: contiguous qadosh forms in chs 40-41 stand at 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses), the bare epithet at oshb:Isa.40.25 against the full title at oshb:Isa.41.14, oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20. items.claim: A parashah division falls after this span's own opening verse at exactly the cut the row names and rejects and is not disclosed, and a cross-seam recurrence is tier-labeled byte although it does not recur in the Hebrew at any tier.
items.evidence: First, the single-witness parashah layer carries a SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.26 (tier-3), a division after this span's opening verse, which is precisely the web:Isa.40.26|web:Isa.40.27 cut the rejected alternative names and dismisses. The row engages that layer, citing the PE at oshb:Isa.40.31, and cites oshb:Isa.40.26 in evidence without its mark, so span-relevant mark symmetry is broken at the one verse where it is decision-relevant. Absence would never be counterevidence, but a mark present inside the span is owed, and here it corroborates the very rival being refused. Second, the byte tier label on the rebuke recurrence is false in both directions: הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21) against oshb:Isa.40.28, and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28) against oshb:Isa.40.21, both return tier NONE: second-masculine-plural imperfect against second-masculine-singular perfect, and the second question of the later verse is introduced by אִם לֹ֣א (oshb:Isa.40.28) rather than by the interrogative particle standing four times in oshb:Isa.40.21. The identity exists only in the English rendering, which translates both openings with the same question pair; the argument does not survive in the bytes. Third, the closing seam is straddled undisclosed: יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.1 at accent_stripped tier, and the reciprocal run יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ (oshb:Isa.41.1) against oshb:Isa.40.31 likewise, a catchword hook at the oracle join which argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed. Secondary: a paseq seg sits at oshb:Isa.40.28 (count-only, single-witness), a verse the row cites in evidence, undisclosed. The two pointed splices are byte tier and the imperative onset at oshb:Isa.40.26 is byte-sound.

items.claim: Two recurrence claims carrying this row's boundary weight are asserted with no Hebrew form, and the one tier-labeled byte is not byte-recurrent.
items.evidence: The opening splice is byte tier and the servant handling is exactly right: the referent is explicit in the bytes and the unnamed-figure zones are left untouched. But the fear-not chain cited at web:Isa.41.10, web:Isa.41.13 and web:Isa.41.14 is stated with no splice and no tier, and it is not one form: אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.41.10) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.13 at accent_stripped tier, while אַל תִּֽירְאִי֙ (oshb:Isa.41.14) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.13 at tier NONE, a feminine-singular form chained with two masculine-singular ones. The second-person fear-verb skeleton, swept contiguous so that both attested spellings are caught under one named object, stands at 4 verses in chs 40-41 (sweep: 4 verses): oshb:Isa.40.9, oshb:Isa.41.10, oshb:Isa.41.13, oshb:Isa.41.14, so the feminine form links this span back to the herald address at oshb:Isa.40.9, not to the two masculine sites the row chains it with. Second, the title claim is tier-labeled byte at three refs with no form quoted anywhere in the row. The count of 3 title verses is correct and correctly excludes the bare epithet at oshb:Isa.40.25, but the three are not byte-recurrent: קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14) reaches only skeleton tier against oshb:Isa.41.16 and against oshb:Isa.41.20, and בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.16) returns tier NONE against oshb:Isa.41.20, whose form is וּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.20); two of the three are prefixed forms and the row names neither. Third, the rejected alternative decides between two single-witness marks by type, ranking the PE at oshb:Isa.41.16 above the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.41.13, loading tier-3 weight the layer does not carry, though a content ground is also supplied. A PE at oshb:Isa.41.20, a ref this row cites, is not disclosed.
